card.name: Emphatic reply words in casual prose
card.fires_on: Short emphatic answer words such as "No", "it" or "now" in informal web writing, often after a rhetorical question or at the end of a punchy clause. The next text is usually a stop or a trailing dot, not a run of exclamation marks.

modes.label: Blunt No answer
modes.description: The word "No" answers a question just asked, often followed by "way", a full stop or a repeat.
modes.example: Life-altering?<< No>>. No. And no. It is

modes.label: Tag-question ending
modes.description: A word near the end of a conversational tag question or a punchy aside, such as "now does it??".
modes.example: doesn’t sound like as much fun<< now>> does it??It also means that you

modes.label: Trailing contrast
modes.description: A word or ellipsis that sets up a turn in the argument, such as "but no…".
modes.example: to unite the two meshes, but<< no>>… such is the injustice of 3

card.writes: It pushes toward smiley or tilde-style casual endings and away from strings of exclamation marks.
card.plain: It marks a chatty, punchy answer word like "No" or "does it" in informal writing.
